title: Stability corridor experiments - SLO onramp sprint brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, cross-functional sprint brief for a 6-week stability onramp pilot we are calling the "Stability Corridor Experiments". The goal is to rapidly validate minimal SLO guardrails, telemetry signals, and rollback mechanics for model-serving feature teams before organization-wide SLO adoption. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — quick experiments, tight measurement windows, and explicit handoffs.

High-level objectives (success criteria):
- Validate a repeatable flow for feature teams to adopt a service-level objective with a 90-day experiment window.
- Demonstrate that three key telemetry signals (p95 latency, p99 latency, and error-rate per-route) can be collected, alerted on, and traced back to a PR within 24 hours on average.
- Show that automated rollback + fallback to a compatible model variant reduces customer-facing error spikes by >= 80% in canary failures.
- Produce a one-page template (runbook + SLO config) that any feature team can use to onboard in < 2 days.

Scope (what we will do in this sprint):
- Apply the corridor experiment to two small-to-medium serving routes: text-generation-primary and chat-reranker-beta.
- Instrument additional telemetry: kv-cache-hit-rate, batch-size-distribution, queueing-depth, and model-variant-fallback-count.

Out of scope:
- Global deployment automation changes beyond config toggles (we will use existing rollout controls).
- Full platform SLO policy rewrite.

Timelines (6-week cadence):
- Week 0 (Prep, owner: Aisha + Jonas): define SLOs, signal definitions, and alerts. Create Linear tickets and link to PRs.
- Week 1 (Instrumentation, owner: Marco): deploy telemetry rows and dashboards. Smoke test with synthetic traffic.
- Week 2 (Baseline collection, owner: Priya): gather 7 days of pre-experiment baseline metrics for both routes.
- Weeks 3-4 (Canary + Controlled Load, owners: feature teams + SRE on-call): run progressive canaries with injected perturbations (latency, N+1 model switch, KV cache miss flood).
- Week 5 (Evaluation & rollback drills): run 3 incident drills where we intentionally trigger fallback and validate automated rollback paths. Capture mean time to detection/rollback.
- Week 6 (Results, template creation, handoff): synthesize learnings, produce onboarding template, and schedule a 60-min cross-functional retro.

SLO definitions (initial):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful responses (2xx/3xx) measured over a 30-day rolling window for each route.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 800ms for inference-only time (excludes pre-processing) over a 7-day window for pilot.
- Error budget policy: stop rollout and revert to previous model-variant when a route exhausts 20% of a 30-day error budget in a 72-hour sliding window.

Signals & telemetry (what to collect):
- Request counts per route (labels: model_variant, region, customer_tier).
- Latency percentiles per route (p50/p95/p99) and histogram for tail analysis.
- Error rate per route and per-model-variant (5xx, infra-timeouts, model-structured-errors).
- KV cache hit rate and cold-start percentage.
- Batching metrics: avg batch size, batch_size distribution, batch wait latency.
- Queue depth and worker saturation (GPU utilization).
- Fallback invocation count and rollback triggers.

Dashboards & alerts (owners: Marco for dashboards, SRE on-call for alert rules):
- Canary dashboard: single-pane with per-route p95/p99, error rate, and rollback events.
- Alert: p99 > 900ms sustained for 10m -> PAGER escalation.
- Alert: route error rate > 0.5% for 5m -> Pager.
- Alert: sudden increase in fallback_invocations (3x baseline in 15m) -> notify #stability-onramp + email to feature team owners.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Project lead: Aisha Kumar — coordination, final decisions on scope changes.
- Instrumentation owner: Marco Ruiz — dashboards, metrics exports, instrumentation PRs.
- Data & evaluation: Priya Patel — baseline calculations, experiment analysis, regression detection.
- Feature team leads: Sofia Nguyen (chat-reranker-beta) and Ethan Park (text-generation-primary) — own route-level changes and coordinating canary traffic.
- SRE on-call rotation: will handle live alerts and run rollback drills during Weeks 3-5.

Experiment designs (examples):
1) KV miss flood: we programmatically mutate KV keys to force a 40% miss rate for 20m during a canary window. Measure latency tail behavior and rollback invocation.
2) Small-batch stress: reduce allowed batch size to 1 for a subset of canary traffic to simulate pathological client patterns.
3) Model-variant degradation: deploy a model variant with a synthetic CPU/GPU slowdown (throttle) to test fallback routing and degradation tolerance.

Rollback & fallback mechanics:
- Canary rule set: start at 0.5% of production traffic, increase to 5% after 30m if no alerts.
- Automated rollback: if error budget trigger fires or p99 breach for > 10m, the canary is automatically aborted and traffic switched back to the last-good model-variant. The action is recorded as a rollback event in the dashboard.
- Manual rollback drill: SRE will execute at least two manual rollbacks during Week 5 to validate runbooks and permissions.

Runbook excerpt (quick steps for an on-call):
1) Receive alert -> join incident channel (#stability-onramp-bridge).
2) Check canary dashboard; confirm whether the issue is limited to canary or global.
3) If canary only: trigger automated abort (button in console) and escalate to feature owner.
4) If global: follow incident major-sev runbook; consider promoted rollback across regions.
5) Post-incident: record root cause, time-to-detect, time-to-rollback, and any missing signals.

Risk register (top items):
- Telemetry lag: if telemetry is delayed >1m we risk false negatives/positives. Mitigation: ensure local synthetic probes and short-window alerts.
- Over-alerting: too sensitive alert thresholds create noise. Mitigation: tune thresholds during Week 1 baseline, add alert suppression for scheduled canaries.
- Permission friction: runbook actions require multiple approvals. Mitigation: create a scoped automation token for rollback during the pilot.

Communications & stakeholder touchpoints:
- Weekly 30-min sync (Mon) with feature leads + SRE + Instrumentation owner.
- Daily 15-min stand during Weeks 3-5 while canaries active.
- Final presentation to product and platform leads at the end of Week 6 (30 minutes + Q&A).

Artifacts to produce at close of pilot:
- 1-page SLO-onramp template (SLO config + alert thresholds + runbook checklist).
- Three dashboards: Canary, Baseline comparison, Postmortem heatmap.
- Short retro note with action items and prioritized backlog for platform improvements.

Open questions we should answer quickly:
- Do feature teams accept the 30-day rolling window for availability SLOs or prefer a 7/14-day pilot window? (decision by Week 0).
- What is the minimum observability retention we need for p99 investigations (7 vs 30 days)?
- Are there any legal/enterprise customers on either route that require separate audit trails for rollbacks?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Aisha: lock decision on SLO windows and share final experiment charter (by 2026-03-18).
- Marco: create initial dashboards and instrumentation PR (by 2026-03-20).
- Priya: kick off baseline data collection job for both routes (start 2026-03-21).
- Feature leads: schedule canary windows on the shared calendar and identify test customers (by 2026-03-19).

Notes & references:
- See Linear SRV-2387 for checklist items and acceptance criteria.
- Telemetry spec doc: confluence link in linked artifacts.
- Slack channel #stability-onramp is the canonical chat during experiments.
